issues.detail: The Greek 'ετοιμον' (prepared/ready) modifies the room ('φώνον'), but the Vietnamese 'đã trải sẵn sàng' (already spread ready) is slightly confusing in its placement. More importantly, the Greek 'ετοιμασατε' is an imperative/command 'prepare' (you prepare), while the Vietnamese 'hãy dọn' (please clean/tidy) changes the specific action of 'preparing' a room to 'cleaning/tidying' it.
